newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey probing nuclear waste claim -- minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey probing nuclear waste claim -- minister.

text.p: Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan said on Thursday an investigation had begun into a former atomic energy official's claim that nuclear waste from Germany was secretly buried and burned in Turkey in the late 1980s.
But Kutan cast doubt on the claim.
"An investigation by the relevant colleagues is under way...I do not believe it possible that anyone would allow this," Kutan told reporters.
"What public official would allow the bringing of dangerous waste from Germany and burying it in Turkey?" Kutan said.
State-run Anatolian news agency quoted a spokesman for the German environment ministry as saying there was no official record of nuclear waste being sent to Turkey.

A former chief of Turkey's Atomic Energy Institute, Ahmet Yuksel Ozemre, was reported on Wednesday as saying that 1,150 tonnes of nuclear waste was buried and 800 tonnes burned in two southern Turkish provinces in 1988-89, when it would have been legal.
The import of dangerous waste into Turkey was banned at the end of 1994.

The Yeni Yuzyil daily quoted Ozemre as saying in a radio interview that the waste was brought to Turkey following his dismissal in 1987 after he himself had rejected foreign requests to dump nuclear waste.
Ozemre did not specify which country the waste had been brought from in the interview, but Yeni Yuzyil said he had previously told a conference the waste had been brought from Germany.
